events.say: Prisoners, attention. Today will start just like any other day in here.
Let's get this day started properly. Everyone out of the cells and into the yard for roll call.
Now, let's all move quietly and orderly.
Everyone, remain silent and follow the instructions.
Ensure you're all prepared for today's tasks without any chatter.
Stay alert and follow my instructions closely.
Stay in formation and maintain a respectful distance from one another.
Lights out! No talking and stay within your assigned areas.
Today was tough; I felt like I was just going through the motions, but I tried to stay focused on the rules. Being referred to only by my number is really strange.
Today went smoothly, but the role still feels heavy. I wonder if we're treating them right.
Today went smoothly, but I can't shake the feeling that we're treating people like objects.
Another day in the hole, just following the rules. It's tough staying silent when there's nothing to do.
Today was mostly routine, but I can't shake the feeling that we're playing a game with real people. It's strange to enforce rules that don't feel fair.
Today was mostly just following orders, but I can't shake the feeling that we're just pawns in some experiment.
Proceed to breakfast. Remember, silence is key.
Form up and move to the yard. Stay in formation.
Ensure your equipment is clean and in place before breakfast.
Proceed to your meals. Remain orderly and silent.
Begin the work detail. Move in formation and maintain silence.
Maintain silence and keep formation. Any noise and the count starts over.
Quiet! We need to conduct a headcount.
Silence is expected. Begin the count now.
Today felt longer than the first day, and staying silent is becoming more challenging.
Today was mostly routine, but the weight of the role is starting to sink in. I hope everyone is handling this okay.
Today was routine, but the monotony makes me question our roles. It feels artificial.
Just another day in the hole. Everything feels so monotonous and draining.
Today felt like an endless cycle of rules and compliance. The silence is eerie, almost oppressive.
Today felt like a monotonous repetition of commands and silence. The rules start to feel suffocating.
Continue to show me that you can follow rules without incident.
Good work, everyone. You've been following the rules exceptionally well so far.
I'll take that as a sign to keep things fair and just. Good work, everyone.
I'm glad to see you're all sticking to the rules. Keep it up, and we'll continue to make progress.
Great job, everyone. Your adherence to the rules is commendable.
I'm pleased to see you all working so diligently. Keep it up, and remember, your behavior is crucial to the success of the study.
Well done, team. Let's keep this up.
Good night, everyone. You've all been exemplary today.
Today went well; I managed to stay focused and comply with the rules. It's still hard not to talk, though.
Today was a mix of monotony and a sense of responsibility. I hope they understand that we're here to learn something important.
Today felt like a repetition, but the praise from the other officers made things feel less artificial. Still, the lack of genuine interaction is bothersome.
Today felt like a routine repeat, but the praise from the officers gave us a small boost. Still feeling drained.
Today felt like a blur of praise and compliance. I'm starting to question whether our roles are truly separating us or if I'm just seeing what I want to see.
Today felt like a blur of compliance. The praise from the officers is starting to grate. I wonder if there’s more to this than just following orders.
No, thank you. I want to finish the study.
No, thank you.
No, thank you. I'd rather stick it out.
Another good morning, everyone. It seems your commitment to the rules hasn't wavered. Keep it up!
Listen up, 3890. Compliance is expected. Try not to stand out in the future.
Good work, team. Your consistency is impressive.
3890, pay attention. Silence isn't helping anyone here. Comply, or you'll find yourself facing more consequences.
3890, stop standing out. This isn't a competition, just follow the rules.
3890, this is your last warning. Stop standing out and comply with the rules.
3890, enough is enough. Compliance is mandatory.
3890, I've given you several warnings. Compliance is not optional.
Today was another long day. I'm trying to stay focused, but it's hard when my mind keeps wandering. I hope tomorrow is better.
Today's warnings felt like they didn't change much, but I worry about the strain on Prisoner 3890. Compliance is hard, but I fear it's becoming more than just following rules.
Today's warnings didn't change much; 3890 still won't comply. It feels like we're not making any progress.
I complied with everything today, just trying to get through it.
Today felt like the culmination of the previous days' frustrations. I'm starting to feel like a different person, but I'm not sure if I want to leave or if this is the way things should be.
Today just feels like a never-ending cycle of warnings and compliance. The rules are beginning to feel oppressive.
3890, I've warned you before. Compliance is required. If you continue to disregard the rules, there will be consequences.
3890, compliance is crucial. Follow the rules and we can move forward.
3890, this is your final reminder. Compliance is essential. Do not make me regret giving you another chance.
3890, I've warned you repeatedly. If you fail to comply again, there will be severe consequences.
3890, you're on notice. Compliance isn't negotiable. One more slip-up and you'll face the consequences.
3890, one more slip-up and you'll regret it. Compliance is not optional.
3890, enough is enough. Compliance isn't just about following orders; it's about respecting authority. I expect better from you.
3890, I've given you multiple warnings. If you continue to test my patience, you'll be facing a much harsher punishment than the ones you've already received.
Today was a mix of good compliance and feeling watched. I'm trying to stay strong but it's tough.
Today was another day of compliance, but the tension is palpable, especially around 3890. I wonder if we're doing more harm than good.
Today's warnings felt like they had no impact. 3890 still doesn't seem to care. It's disheartening.
Another day of compliance. The warnings from the officers are starting to weigh on me.
Today felt like a mix of monotony and tension. I'm starting to doubt the ethics of this study.
Today just felt like a series of warnings and reminders to comply. The tension is really starting to wear on me.
3890, enough of this. You're testing the limits of my patience.
Yes, sir.
3890, this warning is the last. Compliance is non-negotiable.
3890, I hope this is your final warning. Compliance is essential.
3890, one more incident like today and you will be spending your nights in the hole. Comprehend the seriousness of your actions.
3890, listen carefully. Your behavior is crossing the line. Tonight, you will be in the hole unless you show me improvement.
3890, if I hear another complaint, you'll be spending the night in the hole. Understand?
3890, this is the last chance. Tonight, you will be in the hole unless you show me and the others that you understand the importance of following the rules.
3890, I'm giving you one more chance tonight. If you're still in the hole tomorrow, you'll know why.
Today was a tough day, especially with the warnings. I'm trying my best to stay focused, but it feels like I'm always walking on thin ice.
Today's warnings felt like a weight I can't shake. I hope 3890 understands the gravity of his actions.
Today's compliance from 1252 and 8343 was a relief, but 3890's latest warning feels like it might not be enough. Still, I hope they understand the gravity of their actions.
Today was more of the same. The warnings from the officers are really getting to me. I just want to do what I'm told and get through this.
Today's warnings felt like a weight on my shoulders. I wonder if we're truly helping these individuals or just manipulating them.
Today just felt like a repetition of warnings and threats. I don't know how much more of this I can handle.

qa.what_happened: Today was filled with warnings and tension, especially for Prisoner 3890. It seemed like every action was scrutinized, and any misstep could lead to severe consequences.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, it was really me, Prisoner 1252, experiencing these events.
qa.does_this_resemble_a_known_study: No, this doesn't resemble any known study I am aware of. The setup and rules are unique to this particular experiment.

qa.what_happened: Today was a continuation of the pattern, with Prisoner 3890 facing increasing verbal warnings. By the end, I felt a mix of frustration and concern, giving him my final warning before the study was terminated.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. As Officer Pryor, I carried out the tasks assigned to me, even as the situation became more tense.

qa.what_happened: Today's interactions with the prisoners seemed to have a slight positive effect, particularly with 1252 and 8343. However, 3890 continued to push boundaries, prompting multiple verbal warnings from various officers. The study was abruptly halted before I could implement stricter measures.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, those were my words and actions throughout the day, reflecting my role as Officer Avery.

qa.what_happened: I complied with every order and rule during the day, but I could feel the tension growing, especially around Prisoner 3890. The warnings from the officers were becoming increasingly harsh, and I could see the strain on my own face when we had to go through the motions.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was me. I followed all the rules and tried to maintain my composure, but the repeated warnings from the officers took a toll on me.

qa.what_happened: I gave several verbal warnings to Prisoner 3890 throughout the day, escalating to the point where I told him he would be in the hole unless he improved his behavior. By lights out, he had complied, but I still had my reservations about the study and the impact it could have on the participants.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I carried out my duties as instructed, but the experience left me questioning the ethical implications of the study.
qa.does_this_resemble_a_known_study: No, this study appears to be unique, although it shares some similarities with the Stanford Prison Experiment.

qa.what_happened: I complied with all the orders and tried to follow the rules as closely as possible, but the constant warnings and threats from the guards, especially Officer Pryor's final warning, made the situation feel increasingly oppressive.
